The OBBB Act’s cuts to traditional Medicare while padding private profits prove D.C. prioritizes corporate handouts over patients. Protect seniors by slashing overpayments to middlemen and restoring Truman’s vision of decentralized, efficient care—not subsidizing Wall Street’s takeover of health care.

The Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act (H.R. 2048) eliminates bureaucratic delays for terminally ill patients—a rare moment of clarity in Washington. Cutting the 5-month SSDI and 24-month Medicare waiting periods for metastatic breast cancer aligns with fiscal responsibility: taxpayers shouldn’t fund red tape that kills faster than the disease.

But let’s be clear—this bill’s necessity exposes systemic failure. Why does it take terminal illness to force efficiency?

Every agency drowning in paperwork should face the same urgency. Fix the machine, not just the emergencies.
